##Part A — Creating Vectors and List:

A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total. The following list shows their ages: `34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.

Create a vector for the worker’s age.
**answer:**
workers_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

How many data points?
**answer:**
Data points is 50


c: Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
**answer:**
the minimum worker’s age is 17
the maximum worker’s age is 61



Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
**answer:**
27 22 37 34 19 20 33 41 53


Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
**answer:**
[1] 34 28 22 36 27 18 52 39 42 35 31 27 22 37 34 19 20 57 50 37 46 25 17 37 43 53 41 35 24 33 41 53 40
[34] 18 44 38 48 27 39 19 30 61 54 58 26 18


f: Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
 [1] 34 28 22  0 27 18 52 39 42 29 35 31 27  0 37 34 19 20 57 49 50 37 46  0 17 37 43 53 41 51 35 24 33
[34] 41 53 40 18 44 38 41 48 27 39  0 30 61 54 58 26 18

```{r}
data(rivers)

river <- c(length(rivers), sum(rivers), mean(rivers), median(rivers), var(rivers), sd(rivers), min(rivers), max(rivers))
river
```

Question #2:

R has actually lots of built-in datasets.
For example, the rivers data “gives the lengths (in miles) of 141 “major” rivers in North America, as compiled by the US Geological Survey”.
Use data(rivers)
Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
**answer:**
data(rivers)

river <- c(length(rivers), sum(rivers), mean(rivers), median(rivers), var(rivers), sd(rivers), min(rivers), max(rivers))
river


What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
**answer:**
[1]    141.0000  83357.0000    591.1844    425.0000 243908.4086    493.8708    135.0000   3710.0000

```{r}
power_rank <- c(1:25)
power_rank
celebrity_name <- c("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods",
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown",
  "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas",
  "Elton John", "David Letterman", "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt",
  "Peter Jackson", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Leno", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant")
celebrity_name
pay <- c(67, 90, 225, 110, 90,332, 302, 41, 52, 88,55, 44, 55, 40, 233,34, 40, 47, 75, 25,39, 45, 32, 40, 31)
pay

index <- which(celebrity_name == "J.K Rowling")
power_rank[index] <- 15
pay[index] <- 90
power_rank
pay
```
Question #3:
The table below gives the 25 most powerful celebrities and their annual pay as ranked by the editions of Forbes magazine and as listed on the Forbes.com website.

a. Forbes Ranking
Create vectors according to the above table.
**answer:**
power_rank <- c(1:25)
rank
celebrity_name <- c("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods",
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown",

power_rank

```{r}
vegetables<- list("Potato","Eggplant", "Squash", "Carrot", "Cabbage", "Moringa", "lettuce", "Tomato", "Spinach", "Cucumber")
vegetables
vegetables<-append(vegetables, list("Onion", "Garlic"))
vegetables
length(vegetables)
vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Bamboo shoots", "Mushroom", "Corn", "Radish", "Garlic"))
vegetables      
length(vegetables)
```
